Qualified lawfag here - he's getting the standard break. The deal is 11 1/2 to 23 months in county prison (not 2 years) with credit for time served. A very standard offer on a case like this since you need at least two years flat to legally qualify for a state prison sentence. Preliminary hearings are held for a judge to determine whether or not the commonwealth has met its burden to determine if a defendant most likely committed the crime he's accused of - if it's determined he most likely committed any felony, it moves up to the higher court, which Amir0x has already conceded since he waived his preliminary hearing. Expect the next date to be in two weeks for a formal arraignment where the commonwealth just passes their discovery to the defense, then Amir0x will get another two week date for a pre-trial conference where he can formally enter his plea and start serving his sentence.

TL;DR - Amir0x won't be sentenced for at least another month. The judge could even grant immediate parole, but no matter what, he's not serving a single day in state prison. The gravy?
